from_notes: L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986): PRIs constitutionally recognised – a new chapter in the Constitution.
x: The L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) recommended that PRIs be constitutionally recognised, protected and preserved by adding a new chapter to the Constitution; Balwant Rai Mehta did not ask for constitutional status.
source: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 23 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-23.txt) p.15; Laxmikanth, Indian Polity 8th ed. ch.39 Panchayati Raj (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt p.96-100)

from_notes: Official interference reduced to the minimum – to revise and check, not to dictate.
x: Ripon's 1882 resolution wanted official control kept to the minimum – exercised from outside to revise and check, not to dictate; direct State control is the opposite. Elected non-official majorities and suitable sources of revenue were its points, and local staff under the local body fits its aim of autonomy.
source: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India (src/indian-history/spectrum-modern-india.txt p.560-561); PMF Modern History Part 3 (src/indian-history/pmf-modern-history-03.txt) p.392

from_notes: Local self-government is an exercise in democratic decentralisation (UPSC 2017).
x: Local self-government transfers power to elected local bodies, so it is an exercise in democratic decentralisation (UPSC 2017 key); delegation is revocable at will and a confederation is a union of sovereign States.
source: PMF Notes Indian Polity Part 3 (src/polity/pmf-polity-03.txt) p.1 (UPSC 2017 PYQ); NextGen Rocket Sheets Polity Part 1 #37 Local Self-Government (src/polity/rocket-polity-01.txt p.94)

from_notes: What PRIs brought: formal representation of the weaker sections in village governance.
x: PRIs gave weaker sections (SCs, STs, women through reservation) a formal place in village governance; eradicating untouchability, land to depressed classes and spread of education are not what PRIs brought about.
source: app notes 2:79 sub 0; Laxmikanth, Indian Polity 8th ed. ch.39 Panchayati Raj (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt p.96-100) (reservation for SCs/STs/women, 73rd Amendment)

from_notes: L.M. Singhvi Committee called the Gram Sabha the embodiment of direct democracy.
x: In the Gram Sabha all registered voters of the village decide directly; the L.M. Singhvi Committee called the Gram Sabha the embodiment of direct democracy.
source: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity 8th ed. ch.39 Panchayati Raj (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt p.96-100) p.100

from_notes: Why adopted: to decentralise the power of democracy.
x: Panchayati Raj was adopted to decentralise democratic power to elected local bodies – Balwant Rai Mehta's 'democratic decentralisation'; political awareness or educating peasants were not its purpose.
source: Laxmikanth, Indian Polity 8th ed. ch.39 Panchayati Raj (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt p.96-100) p.96; PMF Notes Indian Polity Part 2 (src/polity/pmf-polity-02.txt) p.136 (UPSC 2015 PYQ)

from_notes: Imperium in imperio = 'empire within an empire' – a State within a State.
x: Imperium in imperio means 'an empire within an empire', i.e. a State within a State – a sub-authority with its own sphere inside a larger State; it has nothing to do with State immunity or liability.
source: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 19 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-19.txt) p.6 ('imperium in imperio (empire within an empire)'); Spectrum Modern India p.99

x: Ripon's Resolution on Local Self-Government is dated 18 May 1882 and is called the Magna Carta of local self-government; 9, 11 and 21 May are distractors.
source: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-24.txt) p.9; app notes 2:79 sub 2; Spectrum Modern India p.560
evidence: NextGen Polity 24 p.9 gives only the year 1882
Spectrum p.560 gives 1882; 18 May 1882 is the date of the Government of India resolution (Home Dept.) as cited in standard texts and the app's notes

from_notes: Lord Ripon is called the 'Father of Local Self Government' in India.
x: Lord Ripon, through his 1882 resolution (the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government), is called the Father of Local Self-Government in India; Mayo's 1870 resolution was on financial decentralisation.
source: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-24.txt) p.9; NextGen Rocket Sheets Polity Part 1 #37 Local Self-Government (src/polity/rocket-polity-01.txt p.94)

x: Democratic governance means people share in political power – power rests with the people and is exercised by them or their representatives; officials' participation (c) is administration, not the defining trait, and 'decision making in the hands of public' (d) is only direct democracy.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT Polity Part 1 ch.2 Democracy (src/polity/onlyias-ncert-polity-01.txt); NextGen Rocket Sheets Polity Part 1 #37 Local Self-Government (src/polity/rocket-polity-01.txt p.94) (local accountability, not central control)
evidence: OnlyIAS NCERT Polity 01: democracy = rulers elected by the people, people's share in power
No published official key found; printed key b kept

from_notes: Fundamental objects: people's participation in development and democratic decentralisation (UPSC 2015).
x: The fundamental objects are people's participation in development (I) and democratic decentralisation (III) – UPSC 2015 key 'I and III'; political accountability and financial mobilisation are not.
source: PMF Notes Indian Polity Part 2 (src/polity/pmf-polity-02.txt) p.136 (UPSC 2015 PYQ)

add_option: Both People's participation in development and Democratic decentralisation
x: This is the UPSC 2015 / WBCS 2019 code question with its codes lost: the key is '1 and 3' – people's participation in development and democratic decentralisation together. So neither A nor C alone is the full answer; political accountability and financial mobilisation are not fundamental objects.
source: PMF Notes Indian Polity Part 2 (src/polity/pmf-polity-02.txt) p.136 (UPSC 2015 PYQ); testbook.com WBCS Prelims 2019 official paper (answer 'Both 1 and 3')
evidence: PMF Notes Indian Polity Part 2 (src/polity/pmf-polity-02.txt) p.136 (UPSC 2015 PYQ)

from_notes: Fundamental objects: people's participation in development and democratic decentralisation.
x: The main purpose of Panchayati Raj is people's participation in developmental administration through democratic decentralisation; agricultural output, jobs or political awareness are by-products, not the purpose.
source: PMF Notes Indian Polity Part 2 (src/polity/pmf-polity-02.txt) p.136 (UPSC 2015 PYQ); Laxmikanth, Indian Polity 8th ed. ch.39 Panchayati Raj (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt p.96-100) p.96 (all planning and development activities entrusted to PRIs)

at: To make rural bodies self-sustainable and financially stable
x: The restructured RGSA (approved 2018; 2018-19 to 2021-22, revamped 2022-26) aims to develop the governance capabilities of PRIs so rural local bodies become self-sustainable, financially stable and more efficient (60% central share).
source: Deccan Herald on the Cabinet approval of restructured RGSA (2018); Praveen CA360 May 2026 (src/current-affairs/praveen-ca360-2026-05-magazine.txt) l.1262; myscheme.gov.in/schemes/rgsa

from_notes: Gram Swaraj: Gandhi's self-reliant village republic.
x: Gram Swaraj – the self-reliant village republic – is Mahatma Gandhi's concept (Hind Swaraj, 1909), traced in the Constitution to Article 40; Vinoba Bhave (Bhoodan) and JP (Total Revolution) carried Gandhian ideas forward but did not conceive it.
source: NextGen Rocket Sheets Polity Part 1 #37 Local Self-Government (src/polity/rocket-polity-01.txt p.94) (Art. 40); app notes 2:79 sub 6

x: The words are Mahatma Gandhi's (Young India, 1922): Swaraj would not be a free gift of the British Parliament but India's own self-expression, which an Act of Parliament would merely ratify. Tilak's line was 'Swaraj is my birthright'.
source: Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi vol.22 (Young India, 5 Jan 1922) via mkgandhi.org/momgandhi/chap65.htm ('Swaraj can never be a free gift')

x: Under the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (s.3 explanation), a 'revenue village' is a local area recognised as a village in the revenue accounts after excluding areas in a municipality, cantonment, notified area etc.; so cantonment and municipal areas are excluded, not included.
source: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 (Act 13 of 1994) s.3, indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/16892/1/act_no_13_of_1994_with_footnotes.pdf

x: Participatory budgeting (Porto Alegre model; Kerala's People's Plan) lets citizens deliberate over and directly decide how public resources are spent and opens decision venues to historically excluded groups – all three statements are correct.
source: CDS 2013 official key (d); app notes 2:79 sub 7 (Kerala People's Plan); World Bank / UN-Habitat description of participatory budgeting

x: NMSA (incl. Rainfed Area Development) is a centrally sponsored scheme funded 60:40 by the Centre and general-category States such as Andhra Pradesh (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States) since 2015-16.
source: NMSA operational guidelines, Dept. of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (agricoop.nic.in / nmsa.dac.gov.in); PMF Lens 2026-08-02 (src/current-affairs/pmf-lens-2026-08-02.txt) RAD
evidence: Ministry of Finance, sharing pattern of CSS from 2015-16: 60:40 general States

x: As per AP Water Resources Department records, Andhra Pradesh has 40 river basins (and 81 surface-water sub-basins), the Godavari, Krishna and Pennar being the major ones.
source: AP Water Resources Department book on rivers and streams of AP (inkl.com/news/book-on-rivers-and-streams-in-state-released); IRC WASH groundwater study (Jain 2009)
